edges.description: Shows the increase in number and proliferation of osteogenic front cells that precedes bone invasion of the suture.

nodes.description: As in other craniosynostoses, surgery in infancy excises the fused suture and reshapes the calvaria to stop progression of the deformity and prevent complications of raised intracranial pressure. No MSX2-specific surgical series was found; the evidence is general to craniosynostosis.

evidence.reference_title: Management of craniosynostosis.
evidence.snippet: Treatment for deformational plagiocephaly is conservative when compared with treatment for craniosynostosis, which requires surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Management of craniosynostosis.
evidence.snippet: The principles of surgical intervention are not only to excise the fused suture but also to attempt to normalize the calvarial shape.

nodes.description: Premature fusion of one or more calvarial sutures, the defining feature. Sutural involvement varies widely within families.

evidence.reference_title: Boston type craniosynostosis: report of a second mutation in MSX2.
evidence.snippet: A c.443C>T missense mutation in MSX2, which predicts p.Pro148Leu was identified and segregated with the disease in all affected family members.

nodes.description: In the calvarial sutures, increased MSX2 activity transiently holds back osteogenic differentiation and stimulates proliferation of cells at the advancing osteogenic fronts, so the pool of proliferating osteogenic cells grows. MSX2 also binds RUNX2 and represses its activity; p.Pro148His keeps this repression but escapes its regulation by DLX5.

evidence.reference_title: Msx2 gene dosage influences the number of proliferative osteogenic cells in growth centers of the developing murine skull: a possible mechanism for MSX2-mediated craniosynostosis in humans.
evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that an important early event in MSX2-mediated craniosynostosis in humans is a transient retardation of osteogenic cell differentiation in the suture and a consequent increase in the pool of osteogenic cells.

evidence.reference_title: Ectopic Msx2 overexpression inhibits and Msx2 antisense stimulates calvarial osteoblast differentiation.
evidence.snippet: These results support a model in which Msx2 prevents differentiation and stimulates proliferation of cells at the extreme ends of the osteogenic fronts of the calvariae, facilitating expansion of the skull and closure of the suture.

evidence.reference_title: Regulation of the activity of the transcription factor Runx2 by two homeobox proteins, Msx2 and Dlx5.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, while this mutant form of Msx2 was able to bind to Runx2 and repress its activity, these abilities of Msx2 (P148H) were not subject to regulation by Dlx5.

evidence.reference_title: Boston type craniosynostosis: report of a second mutation in MSX2.
evidence.snippet: These data confirm that missense mutations altering the proline at codon 148 of MSX2 cause dominantly inherited craniosynostosis.

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense variant at proline 148, position 7 of the N-terminal arm of the MSX2 homeodomain (p.Pro148His or p.Pro148Leu). p.Pro148His increases the affinity of MSX2 for its target sequences, by stabilizing the protein-DNA complex, without changing site specificity. MSX2 represses transcription, so the variant is read as enhancing its normal repressor function.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular basis of Boston-type craniosynostosis: the Pro148-->His mutation in the N-terminal arm of the MSX2 homeodomain stabilizes DNA binding without altering nucleotide sequence preferences.
evidence.snippet: we show that the mutation enhances the affinity of Msx2 for a set of known Msx2 target sequences but has little or no effect on the site specificity of Msx2 binding.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular basis of Boston-type craniosynostosis: the Pro148-->His mutation in the N-terminal arm of the MSX2 homeodomain stabilizes DNA binding without altering nucleotide sequence preferences.
evidence.snippet: The enhancement of Msx2 binding is due largely if not entirely to an increased stability of the mutant Msx2-DNA complex.

evidence.reference_title: DNA binding and transcriptional properties of wild-type and mutant forms of the homeodomain protein Msx2.
evidence.snippet: These results provide evidence that Msx2 is a transcriptional repressor and suggest that the mutant form of Msx2 may exert its pathophysiologic effects on craniofacial development by a gain-of-function mechanism.
